$comment: The x86 sheets' typed opcode table: each line as Intel's opcode tables write it (opcode bytes, /r or /n for ModRM, +r / +cc, ib / iw / iz / iv / cb / cz / cp), with the operand size as a parameter: v is 16, 32 or 64 (by mode, the 66 prefix and REX.W), z the immediate's size (16 or 32), sizes the operand sizes a line has per mode (see tools/isa/gen-x86.mjs). Its Intel assembly, the LLVM X86 records it is ({v} {z} {a} {r32} filled in; checked against their opcode, form, operand size, prefixes and immediate), the CPU it came with (since), the modes it exists in, its group, class, description ({size}, {A}, {SP}, ... filled in), pseudocode and flags. The generator makes a row per size, then src/isa/x86.mjs a row per addressing form of a ModRM operand (and per REX in 64 bit mode).
